function: Learns IRS reflection phase shifts (BS runs SLA) and UE transmit power levels (DLPO) to minimise total UE transmit power while meeting rate thresholds. p. 2, 5
system: Single-cell uplink SISO NOMA, single-antenna BS and up to 5 UEs, reflecting IRS with 16 elements and 1-bit phases (0, pi); frequency band not stated. p. 2, 6
method: Game-theoretic distributed learning: SLA (linear reward-inaction) for IRS phases and DLPO (payoff-based) for UE powers; reinforcement-type, online, no neural network. p. 4-5
data_channel: Custom simulation: Rician/Rayleigh gains with path-loss exponents 2 and 2.5, 100 m x 100 m cell, gains static during learning; no dataset or measurements. p. 3, 6
test_conditions: Online learning on the same static channels it is evaluated on; results for varying rate threshold, number of UEs and number of REs; no separate test. p. 6-8
baselines: Random IRS phases followed by DLPO; optimal power allocation without IRS; exhaustive search for the joint problem. No earlier learned method compared. p. 7-8
metrics: Sum utility of UEs versus iterations, action-probability convergence, number of UEs meeting the rate threshold, UE rates and sum transmit power. p. 6-8
q1_support: p. 3: "is the Rician factor between nodes i and j". The channel is the authors' own Rician/Rayleigh model with path-loss exponents from Table I (p. 6); no 3GPP model, public ray-tracing set or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 6: "These gains are assumed to remain static during the course of convergence of the proposed algorithm". No train/test split, transfer or adaptation to unseen conditions is stated; Figs. 6 and 7 only vary the number of UEs and REs.
q3_support: p. 7: "A random phase algorithm, where the phase shifts of the REs are chosen randomly, followed by DLPO" is a variant of the proposed method; the other baselines (optimal power without IRS, exhaustive search) are non-learned. No earlier learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 6: "the number of iterations required for DLPO to converge increases". Only iterations to convergence are plotted (Figs. 2-3), which is not a computational cost; no complexity order, operation count or runtime is reported.
q5_support: p. 6: "We consider a simulation setup similar to [21]". Results come from the authors' own simulation; no code or data link is given and no public dataset is used.
notes: Borderline for no_learning: the learning is tabular and game-theoretic (SLA is based on linear reward-inaction, p. 5; DLPO keeps a state vector updated from received utility, p. 4) with no neural network. Included because agents learn the IRS phases and UE powers from reward feedback; reviewer to confirm, otherwise exclude as no_learning. Area 3 because the learned part sets the IRS phase shifts jointly with UE power. The link is SISO but has an IRS, so the system check passes (p. 2).
